[S] Revisão científica de 2026 no repositório analisa tendências globais do comércio ilegal online de fauna, sem identificar compradores, rotas ou transações ligados a Pretória.

title_en: Eleven mammals seized in online wildlife dealing investigation in Pretoria
fauna_label_en: 11 mammals: 3 lions, 2 tigers, 3 bat-eared foxes and 3 caracals
card_text_en: On 17 November officers in East Lynne seized 3 lion cubs, 2 tiger cubs, 3 bat-eared foxes and 3 caracals; three suspects were detained.
context_en:
[O] A 17 November operation in East Lynne, Pretoria, seized three lion cubs, two tiger cubs, three bat-eared foxes and three caracals — 11 animals — following an investigation of online sale advertisements. Three suspects were detained. Servals were reportedly advertised but were not among the seized animals.

[N] A 2026 International Policy Digest article in news.json examines suspected wildlife-sale listings on digital platforms and the limits of content moderation. This is context for the marketing channel, not evidence that these suspects belong to the networks discussed.

[S] A scientific review indexed in 2026 examines global patterns of online illegal wildlife trade, without establishing buyers, routes or transactions connected to Pretoria.

title_es: Incautan 11 mamíferos en investigación de comercio ilegal digital en Pretoria

card_text_es: El 17/11 se incautaron en East Lynne 3 leones, 2 tigres, 3 zorros orejudos y 3 caracales; tres sospechosos fueron detenidos.
context_es:
[O] Una operación del 17/11 en East Lynne, Pretoria, incautó tres cachorros de león, dos de tigre, tres zorros orejudos y tres caracales —11 animales— tras investigar anuncios de venta por internet. Se detuvo a tres sospechosos. Se habían anunciado servales, pero no figuraban entre los animales incautados.

[N] Un artículo de International Policy Digest (2026), registrado en news.json, examina anuncios sospechosos de tráfico de fauna en plataformas digitales y los límites de su moderación. Aporta contexto sobre el canal comercial, sin vincular a los sospechosos con las redes descritas.

[S] Una revisión científica de 2026 incluida en el repositorio describe tendencias globales del comercio ilegal de fauna por internet, sin identificar compradores, rutas ni transacciones relacionadas con Pretoria.
